correctness.rationale: For non-even P, the largest odd monomial contributes the uncancelled irrational residue -a_r/(sqrt(5))^r at x=alpha^{-r} in E_P'/E_P; algebraic functions have only rational logarithmic residues by Puiseux local valuation. For even P, Binet expansion pairs quadratic Lucas factors with exponents whose denominators divide 5^h. At the largest maximizing coefficient index, the corresponding irreducible Lucas quadratic has an exponent with exact 5-adic valuation -h, forcing the radical extension degree and minimal rationalizing power 5^h by prime-order ramification. The integral examples follow from independently cited published Theorem 1.1. The attached exact-rational checker passed 111 finite factorization and coefficient checks; it is not substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: The accessible primary full text classifies integer-coefficient conditions and proves exact degrees only for monomial weights 5F_n^{2k}; it gives T^6-T^2 as an integral weight without degree. The new theorem provides algebraicity iff even, exact minimal rationalizing power and field degree for every mixed even polynomial, and transcendence for every non-even polynomial. The established monomial case is acknowledged as already covered. Targeted public-record searches and comparisons with accessible scientific claims found no statement whose implication dominates the new classification. Residual risk: unindexed or inaccessible equivalences, including full Minton text not checked.
residual_risks: The full 2014 Minton article was not read; general trace-sequence implications might require comparison with its complete proof.
The full Beukers–Houben–Straub paper was not read, so its higher-dimensional function-field implications were not exhaustively excluded.
An unindexed equivalent degree classification or algebraic-logarithmic-derivative theorem could already yield this special family.

value.rationale: This gives a complete natural invariant of every Fibonacci-polynomial exponential rather than a finite list: transcendence versus algebraicity, rationality and exact degree, with a mixed coefficient 5-adic cancellation criterion. It determines degree 125 for the motivating primary paper's nonmonomial integral example T^6-T^2 and supplies all 5^d for d>=3 among integral weights without common coefficient factor 5. Those distinctions are neither determined by integrality nor by the published single-monomial formula.
